wang2020provably: GCN node classifiers are vulnerable to adversarial edge additions and deletions. The proposed low-pass message-passing approach attenuates such perturbations while propagating features, and it comes with theoretical robustness guarantees in addition to empirical gains. The mechanism can be embedded into existing GCN architectures without redesign. Across graphs and perturbation types it improves accuracy under attack and on clean data, offering provably robust node classification.
wang2021adaptive: Temporal graph networks are powerful but complex, so they overfit noise. MeTA applies data augmentation with adaptive magnitudes: a multi-level memory tower processes augmented graphs of different magnitudes on separate levels and exchanges messages across levels to give each prediction an appropriately augmented input. Three augmentation strategies alter temporal and topological features realistically. Added to popular temporal graph networks without raising time complexity, MeTA improves edge prediction and node classification on standard datasets.
lu2026towards: GNN explainers are unstable on real heterogeneous graphs that contain structural noise. RoHeX first analyzes how heterogeneous architectures amplify perturbations through message passing, then uses denoising variational inference to filter noisy structures and learn robust latent graph representations. Relation-aware semantics are folded into explanation generation as an optimization under the graph information bottleneck, balancing fidelity and compactness. On real heterogeneous graphs it beats state-of-the-art explainers in fidelity, stability under structural perturbation, and semantic meaningfulness.
wang2021curgraph: Graphs vary in classification difficulty, yet GNNs train on them in random order. CurGraph orders training easy-to-difficult: infomax graph embeddings and a neural density estimator score each graph's difficulty from intra- and inter-class embedding distributions, and a smooth-step schedule gradually admits harder graphs. A GNN then trains at the edge of its capability, expanding it each step. Across popular GNNs and graph-classification benchmarks it yields consistent gains.
wang2021mixup: Mixup interpolates features and labels of paired samples, but graph topology is irregular and connected nodes interfere. For node classification, a two-branch graph convolution mixes the receptive-field subgraphs of paired nodes, and a two-stage scheme uses pre-mixup neighbor representations to block cross-pair interference. For graph classification, graphs are interpolated in semantic space. Without raising time complexity, the methods regularize GNNs, improve test accuracy and macro-F1 on standard node and graph benchmarks, and reduce overfitting.
wang2021progressive: GCNs train only on final-layer predictions, forcing every node through one fixed receptive field. ProSup supervises all layers progressively, reweights node losses by hardness estimated along the information flow so the model focuses on hard nodes, and fuses multi-scale hierarchical activations adaptively for the final prediction. Applied to popular GCNs it improves node classification across diverse graphs.
wang2021structure: One-hot labels overconfidently treat every node as purely one class, even when its neighbors in other classes are semantically close, and standard label smoothing ignores graph structure. SALS builds structure-aware label distributions from connected nodes' semantic correlations and replaces one-hot targets, adding no inference cost. On seven transductive and inductive node-classification benchmarks it beats conventional label smoothing and improves strong GNNs.
wang2021time: Temporal graph networks need receptive fields of varying time scales depending on the node and prediction time. TNS learns an adaptive neighborhood per node by interpolating neighbor messages to make discrete neighbor indices differentiable, so sampling is trained end-to-end without extra supervision. It plugs into popular temporal graph networks without added time complexity and improves edge prediction and node classification on standard datasets.
wang2022flashlight: HadamardMLP decoders score edges better than dot-product ones for link prediction, but they cannot retrieve top neighbors in sublinear time, which matters for friend-recommendation-scale services. Flashlight accelerates top-neighbor retrieval by progressively applying approximate maximum inner-product search with adaptively adjusted query embeddings. On OGBL-CITATION2 it speeds inference over 100 times without hurting accuracy, making the more effective HadamardMLP decoder scalable to large graphs.
wang2022graphcache: Sentence-level relation extraction relies on entity types and context that are sparse within a single sentence. GraphCache models these properties across the whole dataset: it propagates features across sentences to learn global entity-type representations and augments each instance's local features with them, treating global priors as a cache that updates online. The module improves relation extraction quality while enabling efficient message passing over all sentences.
wang2022should: Relation extraction exploits entity names but picks up spurious name-relation correlations, and masking names removes useful semantics. CORE builds a causal graph of the extraction model and runs counterfactual analysis to isolate the main effect of textual context from the confounding entity-mention effect, mitigating entity bias at inference without retraining. Model-agnostic, it improves effectiveness and generalization on relation extraction benchmarks.
wang2023causal: Pretrained and large language models rely on biased parametric knowledge of entities, causing unfaithful predictions, and causal debiasing is hard because parameters or logits are inaccessible. A structured causal model with easily estimable parameters supports interventions for both settings: replacing an entity with neighboring entities reduces the specific bias of the original while keeping useful semantics. White-box training-time intervention improves out-of-distribution relation extraction by 5.7 points and machine reading comprehension by 9.1 points, while black-box in-context intervention lifts GPT-3.5 exact match on MRC by up to 20.5 points and cuts entity memorization in RE by up to 17.6 points.
